clusters.mechanism: Catalog add validates only references valid in the old catalog and reads the filtered operator snapshot, so saved references to a re-added model ID are never checked against its new definition, and the next RuntimePolicy startup throws.
manageLocal builds new URL(`http://${host}:8080`) from remote_host without validation or bracketing, so IPv6 or otherwise unparseable hosts throw a raw TypeError and abort the command.
Eval resume passes the stored request and switch chains to strict validators that reject removed model IDs, so legacy evals cannot resume.
retryRun passes the inherited run.models chain through strict validateRunModels, which rejects retired IDs, so historical runs cannot be retried.
Unrequested scope creep beyond the budget, including relaxed catalog-removal rules for terminal runs, a removed remove() guard, and new diagnostics/UI.
The new removed-model tests depend on a missing evals/triage/cases.json fixture, so they fail with ENOENT before exercising model validation.
Old machine-prefixed [local] config keys are silently ignored with no warning.
No end-to-end test covers the CLI mapping of [local].remote_* config keys to manageLocal options.
Runtime models with an undefined provider are loaded and the strict validators do not check provider existence, so new writes can name unroutable models.
Remote host to provider matching requires the base URL to be exactly http://<remote_host>:8080, so enablement is silently not toggled for other setups.
Persisted routing cells naming removed models or model IDs in prefer are now silently dropped with a generic warning, losing the specific startup error, and the guarding test was removed.
